 Order

This petition is filed by the petitioner seeking grant of regular under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. for the offences punishable under Sections 448, 376, 506 and 114 read with section 34 of IPC in Crime No.151/2022 of Mudgal Police Station Dist: Raichur.

Now the charge-sheet is filed in C.C.No.1818/2022.
02.

It is case of the prosecution that, on 03.10.2022 at about 03.00 a.m., when the husband of the complainant had gone to Sheep Market at Sindhanur, the accused No.1 - petitioner had entered into the house of the complainant and caught hold of the complainant, when started screaming, the petitioner put the cloth to her mouth to avoid the screaming and alleged to have committed sexual intercourse.
It is further stated that, the accused No.2 was assisting the accused No.1, by standing outside the house of the complainant and watching the movements of the others.

After the incident,
when the cloth was taken out, which was inserted to the mouth of the complainant, the complainant screamed for help.
On hearing the screaming, the mother-in-law, brother-in-law and father-in-law rushed to her help, by that time, the accused Nos.1 and 2 ran away from the spot.
As such, after consulting the husband of the complainant, the complainant lodged the complaint on 09.10.2022 at about 09.30 a.m.

03. Heard Sri. S. S. Mamadapur, the learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri. Sharanabasappa M.
Patil, the learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent - State.
04. Sri. S. S. Mamadapur, the learned counsel for the petitioner submits that, the petitioner has falsely implicated in this case.
He is innocent for the alleged offences.
There is rival dispute between the family of the petitioner and the complainant.
To take revenge against the petitioner, a false case has been lodged against this petitioner.

It is further submitted that there is contradictory statement given by the complainant in the complaint and the statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.
As such, the petitioner is entitled for bail.
Making such submissions, the learned counsel for the petitioner prays to allow the petition and enlarge the petitioner on bail.

05. Per contra, the learned High Court Government Pleader, by filing statement of objections,
vehemently opposed the bail petition stating that, there are specific overt-acts attributed against the petitioner, who in turn assaulted the complainant sexually, by entering into her house forcibly.
As such, the petitioner is not entitled for any relief as sought for in the petition.

06. Heard the rival contentions of learned counsel for the respective parties and also perused the averments of the charge-sheet.
07.
It appears that prima-facie there is contradiction in the complaint and also the statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.
It is noticed here that, the complainant in the complaint has stated that the accused No.1 committed rape to her.

However, in the statement which was recorded before the Magistrate under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. she has stated that the accused No.1 entered her house at odd hours, at that time she held the petitioner tightly and screamed for help stating that Hanumesh S/O Shankarappa Lambani vs The State Of Karnataka on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82196477/
2 someone entered into the house.

sentences.text: By that time, the in- laws came to the house to help her, the accused No.1 and 2 escaped from the clutches of the complainant.
This contradiction forced this Court to grant bail to the petitioner.

08. Hence, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed.

The petitioner is ordered to be enlarged on bail in Crime No.151/2022 of Mudgal Police Station (pending in C.C.No.1818/2022 on the file of learned Addl. Civil Judge & JMFC, Lingasugur) on executing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/-
(Rupees One lakh only) with one surety for the likesum to the satisfaction of the Trial Court, subject to the following conditions:
a) The petitioner shall appear before the Trial Court regularly without fail.
b) The petitioner shall not tamper nor threaten the prosecution witnesses in any manner.
If in case, the petitioner violates any of the bail conditions as stated above, the prosecution will be at liberty to seek for cancellation of bail.
